description: NVIDIA is fabless; all leading-node GPUs (Hopper H100/H200, Blackwell B200/GB200) are manufactured at TSMC on N4/N3 nodes. NVDA is among TSMC's largest customers.
SK Hynix is the primary HBM3E supplier for NVIDIA H100, H200, and early Blackwell systems. NVIDIA allocates the majority of HBM capacity to SK Hynix.
Micron supplies HBM3E for NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 Blackwell systems, gaining share alongside SK Hynix in the Blackwell generation.
Amkor performs advanced packaging for certain NVIDIA products. TSMC CoWoS is the primary packaging path for high-end AI GPUs.
SMCI builds GPU servers and rack-scale DGX/HGX systems around NVIDIA GPUs. SMCI is the largest NVIDIA system integrator by volume; NVIDIA GPU shipments directly drive SMCI revenue.
Dell PowerEdge AI servers integrate NVIDIA H100/H200/B200 GPUs. Dell is a major NVIDIA AI server ODM partner.
HPE integrates NVIDIA GPUs in ProLiant and Cray supercomputing systems.
AMD is fabless; all leading-node CPUs (EPYC) and AI GPUs (MI300X, MI325X) are manufactured at TSMC on N4/N3 nodes.
SK Hynix supplies HBM3E for AMD MI300X and subsequent Instinct AI GPUs.
Micron supplies HBM for AMD Instinct AI GPU series, competing with SK Hynix.
Broadcom is fabless for leading-edge products; custom AI ASICs (XPU) and networking silicon are manufactured at TSMC.
Marvell is fabless; custom AI ASICs and networking silicon are manufactured at TSMC on N5/N3 nodes.
Qualcomm is fabless; Snapdragon mobile SoCs and Snapdragon X PC chips are manufactured at TSMC.
ASML EUV systems are required for TSMC N3/N2 node production. TSMC is ASML's largest customer. EUV system delivery schedule is a gating factor for leading-node capacity ramp.
ASML supplies EUV systems to Intel Foundry for 18A/14A node ramp. Intel is a major ASML customer for both EUV and High-NA EUV.
ASML supplies EUV systems to Samsung Foundry and Samsung memory for leading-edge DRAM.
Applied Materials supplies deposition, etch, and CMP equipment to TSMC for all process nodes.
Applied Materials supplies deposition and process equipment to Intel Foundry.
Applied Materials supplies equipment to Samsung for both foundry and memory manufacturing.
Lam Research supplies etch and deposition equipment to TSMC. Critical for advanced node patterning.
Lam Research supplies etch equipment critical for SK Hynix HBM and DRAM manufacturing.
Lam Research supplies etch and deposition equipment to Micron for DRAM and HBM manufacturing.
KLA supplies process control and inspection equipment to TSMC for yield management at all nodes.
Google co-designs TPU AI accelerators with Broadcom. Broadcom is the primary manufacturing and packaging partner for Google TPU v4/v5. This is among Broadcom's largest revenue relationships.
Meta is developing MTIA custom AI inference chips with Broadcom as the silicon partner.
Marvell supplies custom networking ASICs to Amazon AWS and is a design partner for AWS custom silicon programs.

Microsoft Azure is the largest external buyer of NVIDIA AI GPUs. Azure GPU cluster buildout (H100, H200, B200) drives significant NVIDIA data center revenue. Microsoft capex guidance is a leading indicator for NVIDIA.
Meta is one of the largest buyers of NVIDIA H100/B200 GPUs for Llama model training and recommendation system inference.
AWS purchases NVIDIA GPUs for EC2 P5 instances (H100) alongside custom Trainium silicon.
Google buys NVIDIA GPUs for GCP A3 instances and research workloads, alongside custom TPUs.
Microsoft Azure is among Arista's largest customers for data center spine/leaf Ethernet switching. Azure AI cluster networking expansion drives Arista revenue.
Meta uses Arista switches extensively in data center fabric. Meta AI cluster networking expansion is a demand driver.
AWS uses Arista in portions of its data center networking alongside custom merchant silicon.
Microsoft Azure procures AI GPU servers from SMCI for Azure AI deployments.
AWS procures GPU servers from SMCI alongside direct ODM relationships.
Microsoft data centers use Vertiv power and cooling infrastructure. AI GPU density increases drive liquid cooling demand from Vertiv.
AWS data centers use Vertiv UPS, PDUs, and cooling systems. Growing AI workload power density accelerates Vertiv procurement.
Google data centers rely on Vertiv for power and thermal management, with liquid cooling requirements increasing with TPU and GPU deployments.
Arista switches use Coherent optical transceivers for inter-rack and inter-DC connectivity. 400G/800G transceiver demand is driven by Arista customer data center buildouts.
SMCI GPU servers and HGX baseboard systems are built around NVIDIA GPU modules. SMCI revenue is highly correlated with NVIDIA GPU availability and pricing.
